title: EC2 and EBS: when you own the machine
outcome: Explain instance lifecycle, disk persistence, process supervision, and the responsibilities EC2 leaves with you.
useCase: Understanding existing VM deployments and choosing compute ownership.
drawbacks: Patching, configuration drift, and recovery remain your work.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: A machine is replaceable only if its important state is accounted for.

trace.title: Image and instance
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

EC2 gives you virtual machines. You choose an image, instance capacity, network, identity, and storage.

You still own operating-system patching, process configuration, application deployment, and much of the recovery plan.

An instance is not the same thing as a persistent data store. EBS volumes have their own lifecycle and zone attachment rules; instance-store data is a different contract.

A Rails app should not treat its local upload directory as shared storage across several instances.

Training setup: select a deliberate image/type, attach a narrow instance role, use controlled management access, configure security groups, supervise the app process, send logs off the machine, and test replacing the instance.

Keep the database and uploads in services with explicit persistence/backup policies.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Boot image → inject configuration/identity → start supervised process → health check → receive traffic.

Replacement should recreate the application from its artifact/configuration, not depend on manual edits left on the old machine.

Scale to two instances and follow an upload/read. If only one instance has the file, the storage boundary is wrong for that architecture.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A manually repaired server becomes hard to reproduce. A successful reboot is not a tested restore.

Local logs disappear with the machine if not collected.
